newsitem.title: INDIA: Bank of India IPO opens, seen scraping through.
newsitem.headline: Bank of India IPO opens, seen scraping through.

text.p: State-run Bank of India's initial public offering of 150 million shares to raise 6.75 billion rupees opened on Friday amid poor retail interest in the issue, brokers and analysts said.
"The response is very poor at the retail level," said a primary market dealer at a Bombay brokerage.
Brokers said the issue would scrape through as financial institutions, mutual funds and some expatriate Indians were showing interest in subscribing to the issue.
"Institutions are interested because it is cheap," said a broker. Bank of India's issue price is 45 rupees for a 10-rupee face value share.
"They find it cheaper than HDFC Bank," said a broker, explaining institutions' buying interest in Bank of India.
Shares of the private HDFC Bank were trading at 46 rupees a share at noon on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
Shares of Dena Bank, another state-run bank, were listed earlier this year at less than its offer price, analysts said.
Analysts said Bank of India priced the issue low in view of uncertain market sentiments and made its issue attractive by asking for only 25 rupees to be paid with share applications.
The balance would be collected at a later date.
Some Indian companies, especially clients of Bank of India, are expected to subscribe to the issue, analysts said.
The bank had written to companies - its clients and non-clients - seeking support for its IPO.
P.S. Shenoy, Bank of India's general manager, said he expected the issue to be oversubscribed by 2.5 times.
DSP Merrill Lynch, a lead manager to the issue, said Bank of India had a pre-dominant position in semi-urban and rural India, which gave it access to stable and low-cost deposits.
"This will provide a good hedge against emerging competition in the urban markets," said Arpit Agarwal, assistant vice president at DSP Merrill Lynch, affiliate of the U.S. firm.
Bank of India is the country's third largest bank in terms of deposits, advances and total assets, DSP Merrill said.
The issue is meant to augment the net worth for meeting future capital adequacy requirements and to widen the shareholder base, the bank said. It is now fully government-owned.
The issue closes on February 28, the day when the government unveils its budget for 1997/98 (April-March).
Bank of Baroda shares were listed on the BSE on Friday but trading was suspended by the exchange minutes after it began in view of confusion from continuous listing of partly- and fully-paid shares.
